Estimate a directed relative-importance network

Source: R/relimp.R
relimp_network.Rd

relimp_network() estimates a directed relative-importance network: for each variable, how much of its variance the other variables explain together and how that explained variance is shared among them. Each variable is regressed on all the others, and its \(R^2\) is divided among the predictors by the LMG method (Lindeman et al., 1980; Groemping, 2006): a predictor's share is its increase in \(R^2\) when it enters the regression, averaged over all orders in which the predictors can enter, which is the Shapley value of the predictor.

The shares are non-negative and sum to the \(R^2\). The network is directed: the edge from a predictor to an outcome carries the predictor's share of the outcome's explained variance, so the two edges between a pair of variables can differ. relimp_network() computes these shares for every variable from raw data or a correlation matrix. With normalized = TRUE each outcome's shares are rescaled to sum to 1, giving proportions of explained variance rather than proportions of total variance. The computation considers every subset of predictors, so its cost doubles with each added variable; max_nodes limits the network size.

It returns the network of shares; the identity that defines the decomposition is checked by certificate().

For undirected conditional associations use ebic_glasso() or pcor_network(). The shares are those of relaimpo::calc.relimp(type = "lmg") applied to each variable in turn.

Usage

relimp_network(
  data = NULL,
  cor_matrix = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  cor_method = c("pearson", "spearman", "kendall", "auto"),
  max_nodes = 21L,
  normalized = FALSE,
  na_method = c("pairwise", "listwise"),
  labels = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A numeric data frame or matrix with one row per observation. Not needed when cor_matrix is given.

cor_matrix

A correlation matrix to use instead of data; it must be symmetric and positive semi-definite, and a covariance matrix is rescaled to a correlation matrix.

n

Accepted and ignored: the decomposition needs only the correlation matrix. It exists so that a call written for the other estimators, (cor_matrix = , n = ), also works here.

cor_method

Correlation computed from data: "pearson" (default), "spearman", "kendall", or "auto" (polychoric and polyserial correlations for ordinal items; see cor_auto()).

max_nodes

Largest number of variables accepted, a whole number >= 2. Default 21; larger networks are refused.

normalized

Whether to rescale each outcome's incoming shares to sum to 1, as bootnet and relaimpo report them. Default FALSE, which keeps shares that sum to the outcome's \(R^2\).

na_method

Handling of missing values in data: "pairwise" (default) or "listwise". See ebic_glasso().

labels

Optional node labels, one unique label per node of the network.

Value

A fitted network of class psychnet (psychnet), directed, whose edge weights are importance shares. as.data.frame() returns one row per edge with columns from (the predictor), to (the outcome) and weight; certificate() reports the structural check. The object also stores each node's full-model \(R^2\) (r2), the correlation matrix (cor_matrix), whether the shares were normalized (normalized) and, with normalized = TRUE, the unscaled shares (raw_importance), from which the certificate is computed. The sample size is recorded when the network is built from data and is NA with cor_matrix.

Details

The \(R^2\) of each subset regression is computed from the correlation matrix. The certificate, computed by lmg_certificate(), checks that each outcome's shares sum to its full-model \(R^2\) and that this \(R^2\) agrees with its closed form from the inverse correlation matrix.

Conditions

psychnet_bad_input when there are more variables than max_nodes, max_nodes or normalized is invalid, cor_matrix is not a finite, symmetric, positive semi-definite matrix with a positive diagonal, or labels do not match the nodes; psychnet_constant_variable (warning) when a constant or all-missing column is dropped.

References

Lindeman, R. H., Merenda, P. F., & Gold, R. Z. (1980). Introduction to bivariate and multivariate analysis. Scott, Foresman.

Groemping, U. (2006). Relative importance for linear regression in R: The package relaimpo. Journal of Statistical Software, 17(1), 1-27. doi:10.18637/jss.v017.i01

See also

lmg_certificate() and certificate() for the check; ebic_glasso() and pcor_network() for undirected networks; psychnet(), which routes method = "relimp" here; psychnet for the result.

Examples

S <- 0.4^abs(outer(1:5, 1:5, "-"))
relimp_network(cor_matrix = S)
#> <psychnet> relimp network
#>   nodes: 5   edges: 20   (directed)
#>   structural certificate (decomposition residual): 5.55e-17
